people.name: Pip
people.role: Juvenile sapient orchard mimic adopted by Jayson as his daughter. In Chapter 14 she bonded rapidly with Mela, helped teach her language and play, travelled to Sari's family village, received a tiny hero cape, and began growing quickly enough to nearly outgrow her drawer-bed.

people.name: Nyx / Death
people.species: Primordial Cosmic Entity / Cheetah Felari disguise
people.role: The literal embodiment of Death and one of the Four Riders. In Chapter 14 she supported the vivarium aftermath, explained the difference between delaying a soul and true resurrection, revealed her identity to Sari, and continued living publicly as a university student in Room 14.

people.name: Taren
people.role: Young Wolfkin student subjected to sustained intimidation by other students. Jayson helped and healed him, encouraged his growing connection with Mira, and later introduced them properly to the group.

people.name: Mira
people.role: Confident Wolfkin student close to Taren and possible developing romantic interest. She supported him after his confrontation and later met Jayson's group properly in the market.

people.name: Cael Vorr
people.role: Advanced Axiomatic adjudication student who regarded Pip as vermin and deliberately threw a magically charged dining spike at her. Jayson intercepted it and restrained him; Aureliane charged him with attempted murder and related offences.

people.name: Sari
people.role: Young Transcendent House student and Mela's mother. Jayson rescued her from an attempted assault and abduction, later discovered her dorm room had been used as a conspiracy cache because she was considered unlikely to be believed, and temporarily sheltered her in Room 13.

people.name: Mela
people.role: Sari's juvenile orchard mimic daughter. Rescued and healed alongside Sari, formally registered as Sari's dependent child and person, and rapidly became close friends with Pip.

people.name: Adjunct Serik Vaul
people.role: University adjunct identified as a central figure in the hidden vivarium network involving illegal experiments, altered consent, captive Beastfolk, and juvenile mimics.

people.name: Lecturer Halven
people.role: University lecturer connected to the hidden cache in Sari's room and the wider Vaul conspiracy. Jayson baited him into incriminating himself, subdued him, and delivered him to Aureliane.

people.name: Tomas (University Student)
people.role: University student caught attempting to recover the conspiracy cache hidden in Sari's dorm room. Captured and handed over to Aureliane. Distinct from the Chapter 1 thief also named Tomas.

people.name: Veyr
people.role: University student and accomplice of Tomas who helped attempt to recover the hidden cache from Sari's dorm room.

people.name: Raska
people.role: Person identified as a potential target during the wider investigation, leading to discussion of using false location information to expose information leaks.

people.name: Varr
people.role: Person involved in the dangerous-animal and underground-channel investigation Jayson assisted with.

people.name: Sela
people.role: Person involved in the dangerous-animal and underground-channel investigation alongside Varr.

people.name: Fellan
people.role: Guilded Path worker who insulted Sari and Mela and treated them with open racial contempt.

people.name: Borru
people.role: Guilded Path portal attendant who managed the storm-damaged route toward Kharveth Hollow.

people.name: Rhuva
people.role: Sari's mother and Mela's grandmother. A formidable, affectionate Wolfkin woman and excellent cook who immediately accepted Mela as family.

people.name: Dhorrek
people.role: Sari's father and Mela's grandfather. A quiet timber worker and woodworker with old scars and chronic knee trouble.

people.name: Keshran
people.role: Sari's older brother and Mela's uncle. A teasing trail-runner and village patrolman who helps protect the surrounding foothills.

people.name: Tovrek
people.role: Neighbour from Sari's foothill village who loudly announced Sari's return.

people.name: Veskara
people.role: Vulpanii tailor in Valenhold's Grand Clothiers' Arcade. She outfitted the group, made tiny hero capes for Pip and Mela, recognized Jayson's unusual fox nature, and offered to contact Elder Shaveth about old many-tailed fox-spirit stories.

people.name: Solstice
people.role: Nyx's ancient independent companion and the horse associated with Death.

Chapter 1: Jayson's wives are missing and separated from him; finding and reuniting with them is his overriding personal goal.
An unknown surveillance and indexing group is profiling Jayson and developing containment or management contingencies.
Organized experimentation involving Listeners remains unresolved.
Watcher entities and their hidden infrastructure remain poorly understood.
Some hidden structures may be remnants of extremely ancient advanced technology.
Systemic racism, enslavement, exploitation, kidnapping, and trafficking of Beastfolk remain major threats across Eryndor.
The Watchtower Orchard planar anomaly, strange lights, and abnormal time effects remain unexplained.
Chapter 2: Marlen Voss has been exposed as a Guild mole, but investigators are using her to trace the wider trafficking network.
The full extent of the Beastfolk trafficking network remains unknown.
Possible corruption or information leakage within the Adventurers' Guild remains unresolved.
The Westbridge front desk clerk remains a suspicious but unproven lead.
Liri's home and family remain unresolved, and Jayson intends to help return her safely.
Chapter 3: The Chapter 3 roadside ambush may connect to the larger surveillance, trafficking, or Guild-related threats.
Kestrel's hidden past and the identity of Thrennael remain unresolved.
Jayson continues searching for a way to properly study magic and recover his lost powers.
Fleas's nature, development, and connection to Jayson's fifth tail remain unexplained.
Chapter 4: Jayson's distrust of the gods deepens over the forced separation from his wives.
Liri's half-Kitsune heritage may expose her to an unknown force capable of detecting or hunting Kitsune.
Fleas is concealing Liri from the unknown force searching for Kitsune.
Ishen proves that Jayson is not the first extraplanar Kitsune known to have reached Eryndor.
Eryndor's cosmological state appears fundamentally abnormal, but the cause remains unknown.
The deeper significance of the Anchor Ring remains unknown.
Chapter 5: A higher observer beyond gods and Watchers may threaten Jayson's wives if they become directly observable.
The relationship between the various hidden groups, ambushes, surveillance networks, trafficking operations, and clandestine actors remains unresolved.
Watchers may be ancient maintenance or enforcement systems operating on obsolete protocols.
A recovered spider-like device proves that advanced lost technology remains active or in circulation.
Jayson suspects modern Eryndor sits atop the remains of a far older technologically advanced civilization.
Possible ancient Earth-Eryndor contact or migration remains unproven.
Irix's true history, origins, capabilities, and connection to hidden systems remain unknown.
Deepreach / The Vertical may connect to Eryndor's deepest surviving systems and remains a major long-term objective.
Chapter 6: Irix's Ashen Serathi lineage and its cultural significance remain incompletely understood.
Irix is a continuity anchor, but the nature, limits, and purpose of that ability remain unknown.
A professional network of Continuity Hunters is actively seeking Irix.
The Copper Finch Observer survived and may report Jayson's warning back to Irix's hunters.
Jayson has entered Irix's conflict directly by opposing and threatening to pursue those hunting her.
Chapter 7: The long-term consequences of the Chapter 7 high-rank adventurer confrontation remain unresolved.
Jayson's Spark abilities Hearthbound and Heatwave remain incompletely explored.
Jayson's mana-circuit and holographic projection experiments may have major technological and magical implications.
Jayson's ambient-mana purification method can produce extremely pure mana and remains secret.
Jayson's presence-damping micro-engraving may function as perceptual omission or practical invisibility.
The University of Magic becomes an active path toward knowledge, training, and possibly restoring Jayson's power.
Chapter 8: The University may take special interest in Jayson's abnormal observational ability, restraint, and threat assessment.
Chapter 9: Jayson's abnormal entrance scores, unresolved magical capacity, and existential stability readings make him an institutional anomaly.
House assignments risk dividing Jayson, Kestrel, and Irix despite their commitment to remain a unit.
Riven and Sael may become part of a broader Beastfolk support network within the University.
University surveillance and ward-based behavioral logging are extensive.
Jayson's belief-state manipulation may exploit passive truth and intent detection.
The University libraries and restricted archives may provide answers about magic, lost technology, and Jayson's condition.
Chapter 10: Cognitive casting may provide a path toward restoring or reconnecting Jayson's lost power.
Irix may eventually transfer Houses through formal procedures or demonstrated incompatibility.
Jayson possesses hidden failsafes unknown to the gods; their nature and consequences remain unresolved.
The goddess's warning about administrative containment and dependency raises questions about University intentions.
Chapter 11: Jayson is spiritually bound to seven wives through literal heartstrings whose full nature and implications are still being understood.
Jayson's temporal resets now occur in Eryndor; their trigger, mechanism, and controlling force remain unknown.
One reset branch proved Jayson's former power can potentially be restored.
University wards can detect at least some effects of Elandria's dream intrusions.
Jayson and Elandria's relationship remains damaged by his displacement, his wives' separation, and her continued interference.
Irix's assault and delayed reporting expose unresolved tensions around autonomy, protection, and when intervention is appropriate.
Irix is beginning to build independent friendships and support outside Jayson and Kestrel.
Jayson's passive condenser can produce pure white mana while its true function remains concealed from the University.
Chapter 12: Jayson has begun a major unrevealed design project in the University Archives.
Chapter 13: Elandria's private divine realm, household, mimic nursery, and ancient stables reveal a much larger divine ecosystem than previously known.
Nyx is literal Death, one of the Four Riders, and is living incognito as a university student.
Nyx's Triune Scholar status raises questions about how much the University and Aureliane understand about her.
Nyx's true identity must remain tightly contained because wider disclosure could have severe consequences.
War, Pestilence, and Famine remain largely unknown.
Pip's growth, language, mimic abilities, legal recognition, and eventual independence remain long-term arcs.
Pip's existence raises a broader question of mimic personhood and legal recognition.
The legal and institutional consequences of Cael Vorr's attempted murder of Pip remain unresolved.
Whether Aureliane can address systemic institutional prejudice rather than only individual offenders remains unresolved.
Taren's harassment and growing connection with Mira may develop independently.
Jayson, Kestrel, Irix, Pip, and Nyx are developing into a broader chosen-family unit.
Chapter 14: Jayson's larger purpose in Eryndor increasingly centers on repairing the world while finding a path back to his power and home.
Nyx has distinguished delaying a departing soul from true resurrection, leaving the limits of actual resurrection unresolved.
Mela's rapid development, mimic biology, future abilities, and legal treatment remain active arcs.
Sari and Mela need a safe long-term living arrangement after Sari's dorm was compromised.
The Lower Vivarium has been exposed, but the Vaul conspiracy extends to unidentified higher participants.
Halven, Tomas, Veyr, and other captured conspirators may lead investigators toward higher members of the Vaul network.
Witnesses connected to the vivarium exposure may become retaliation targets.
Aureliane has become an investigative ally while restricting Jayson from independently pursuing suspects.
Aureliane's spatial-folding abilities may provide a future lead toward dimensional travel.
Veskara's connection to Elder Shaveth may uncover older Vulpanii records of many-tailed fox spirits.
Old Vulpanii stories may describe an earlier Kitsune or extraplanar fox-man in Eryndor.
Vulpanii history may provide a cultural and historical bridge to Jayson's Kitsune origins.
Veskara and Shaveth may provide a second independent line of evidence for earlier Kitsune contact with Eryndor.
Jayson and Sari's increasingly flirtatious friendship may develop further, though no romance is established.
Dhorrek's chronic knee problems remain a possible future healing thread.
